label: Reagan Embraces Communist Economics
detail: The President publicly champions state ownership of industry and central economic planning in the final days of the campaign.
assumption: Voters respond to the incumbent's declared turn toward state ownership and central planning as a sharp break with his record and party; the effect is strongest among his conservative, business-oriented and anti-communist supporters and among Cold War-minded voters.
facts_text: The party of the administration in office since 1981, which also holds a majority in the Senate, has been thrown into turmoil by the President's statements.
Leaders of the party that held the presidency from 1977 to 1981 and holds a majority in the House have said they do not share the President's economic program.
nominee_news: He has called for public ownership of major industries and central planning of prices and wages.
He has said the government should take a leading role in directing the nation's economy.

add_planks.text: Expand government ownership of major industries and adopt central planning of the economy.

research_questions: How did conservative and anti-communist voters behave when a party's nominee abandoned core economic positions?
How did Cold War-era voters react to candidates accused of being sympathetic to communism?
How often did partisans defect to the opposing nominee or stay home when their own nominee broke with party ideology?
source_text: ronald reagan advocated for communist economic policies
